newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Asia Product Swap - Pressure remains on gas oil.
newsitem.headline: Asia Product Swap - Pressure remains on gas oil.

text.p: Singapore gas oil swaps edged down slightly late afternoon on Thursday despite some bargain hunting as the market is still weighed down by concerns of a prompt physical overhang, traders said.
"Gas oil is still under pressure. I don't see the market bottoming yet because there are no big demand out there," a trader said.
July swaps were last quoted at $19.90/$20.00 per barrel down about 10 cents from Wednesday when prices closed down a hefty $1.00 from the previous day.
August was quoted at $20.90/$21.00 up about 10 cents from Wednesday which has led to a widening to the time spread.
July/August was last valued at minus $1.00 from about 90 cents on Wednesday.
Traders said the downward pressure remains because the region's two big buyers China and India are not buying in a big way.
Traders said large Chinese diesel purchases are not likely due high stocks and poor domestic demand which has forced authorities to stop issuing fresh import licenses.
India had bought a meagre 165,000 tonnes of diesel for August delivery compared to the 855,000 it bought for July arrival.

In the physical market offers hit a low of $19.80 per barrel a sellers scrambled to get rid of prompt cargoes. Despite the low offer, 50 cents below Wednesday's lowest offered level, no buyers emerged.
The swaps jet fuel market firmed with the jet/gas oil regrade up about 10 cents at $1.90/$2.10 for July with one lot traded at $2.00 earlier in the day.
The firmer regrade was due to the sharp falls to gas oil prices, brokers said.
Physical jet fuel was lower on Wednesday trading earlier at $22.10 per barrel and later at $21.85, both for July 24-28 liftings, free-on-board (fob) basis.
Fuel oil swaps rose along with the firm physical market which in turn has been receiving good buying support.
July was quoted at $99.25/$100.25, up from Wednesday's $98.50/$99.25.
